title: The Lion and the Mouse
text:
A lion lay asleep in the shade when a little mouse, running across the ground, scampered over his face and woke him. The lion clapped a huge paw down on the mouse and opened his jaws to swallow it.

The mouse begged for its life. "Let me go," it squeaked, "and one day I may be able to repay you." The lion found the idea so funny that a mouse could ever help the king of beasts that he laughed, lifted his paw and let it run off.

Some time later hunters set a trap in the forest, and the lion walked straight into it. A net of thick ropes dropped over him, and the more he struggled, the tighter it held. His roars of rage and fear echoed through the trees.

The mouse recognized the voice and ran toward it. Finding the lion tangled and helpless, it set to work with its sharp little teeth and gnawed through one rope after another until a hole opened in the net. The lion pushed his way out and went free. "You laughed at me," said the mouse, "but now you know that even a mouse can help a lion."
lesson: Treat people kindly whatever their size or status. You cannot know today who will be the one able to help you tomorrow.
